title: Noor and the Wolf Anew
premise: Yara Eriksen, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-outlawed city of Vellmark, is unmasked when a royal purge sweeps the streets. Hunted by the crown and haunted by the wolf-god Fenris, whose broken covenant once bound storm to stone, Yara flees north with a disgraced royal inquisitor, Soren Vale, who begins to question everything he serves. To survive, Yara must reforge the covenant between human and wolf realms—an act that demands either their magic or their life—and discovers the crown's hunt is a cover for draining the land's wild power for the king's immortality. In the end, Yara chooses love over duty by sharing the covenant's price with Soren and the freed wolf-kin, toppling the king but losing their exile forever: they become the living bridge between realms, seen at last.
about_author: August Iversen is the pen name of a former folklorist who spent a decade collecting storm songs along the northern coasts before turning to fantasy. They write about outsiders, old bargains, and the weather of the heart from a cabin that is, allegedly, never struck twice.

chapters.title: Charms for a Rainless City
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In outlawed Vellmark, Yara sells harmless trinkets while secretly calming storms for desperate neighbors, keeping their gift buried for twenty years. A small act of magic saves a child but leaves frost on the windowpanes. Emotional beat: the ache of a life lived small.

chapters.title: The King's Proclamation
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Criers announce a realm-wide hunt for the gifted; neighbor turns on neighbor. Yara's oldest friend begs them to run, but Yara hesitates, unwilling to abandon the hidden community they protect. Emotional beat: dread hardening into stubbornness.

chapters.title: Frost on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Soren's POV. Royal inquisitor Soren Vale traces the frost-magic to Yara's shop but finds only a frightened shopkeeper and a child's drawing of wolves. He lies in his report—his first lie. Emotional beat: a crack in certainty.

chapters.title: The Wolf That Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In dreams, the wolf-god Fenris speaks for the first time in twenty years, showing Yara the covenant's breaking and warning that the hunt is harvesting the gifted, not imprisoning them. Emotional beat: terror braided with longing.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Night Market
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The inquisition burns the night market; Yara's friend is taken. Yara unleashes a storm to cover the escape of three gifted children, revealing themselves fully. Emotional beat: grief detonating into open rebellion.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Choice
chapters.summary: Soren's POV. Ordered to execute captured gifted, Soren instead frees them and goes rogue, finding Yara bleeding in the ruins. Neither trusts the other, but both need the road north. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, mutual shame.

chapters.title: Northward, Against the Wind
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The fugitives cross the moorlands toward the Wolf Reaches, pursued by Soren's former protégé, Captain Ilse Brandt. Yara teaches Soren to read weather; he teaches her court secrets. Emotional beat: wary respect kindling.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At a drowned shrine, Yara recovers a fragment of the old covenant-stone and learns the ritual requires a willing sacrifice from each realm. Soren overhears and says nothing. Emotional beat: the weight of a secret kept out of mercy.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Magic
chapters.summary: Soren's POV. A village that betrayed its own gifted generations ago now starves, its fields dead. Yara heals the land at great cost, and villagers kneel—not to them, but to the idea of magic again. Emotional beat: hope as a dangerous contagion.

chapters.title: Ilse at the Ford
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Captain Brandt corners the fugitives at a river crossing. Soren offers his surrender in exchange for the others' freedom; Ilse, once his friend, wavers. Yara's storm scatters the soldiers anyway. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against conscience.

chapters.title: The King's Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Soren's POV (flashback interwoven). We learn the king has been drinking distilled magic for decades, hollowing himself into something ageless and hungry—the true purpose of the hunt. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything.

chapters.title: First Snow, First Truth
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Snowbound in a shepherd's hut, Yara tells Soren the full truth of their exile—they broke the covenant fleeing a forced sacrifice twenty years ago. Soren confesses he knew, and stayed silent. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in confession.

chapters.title: The Wolf Reaches
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They reach the border where the world smells of pine and old blood. Wolf-kin sentries take them captive; among them is Ravn, a wolf-blooded woman who remembers Yara's mother. Emotional beat: homecoming to a place that may not forgive.

chapters.title: Judgment of the Pack
chapters.summary: Ravn's POV. The pack council tries Yara for the covenant's breaking. Evidence shows Yara was a child pawn of human lords, not a traitor—but the price of renewal remains unchanged: one life freely given. Emotional beat: justice without comfort.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Yara prepares to die for the covenant; Soren secretly negotiates to take their place, arguing a human life balances a human betrayal. They quarrel bitterly—each claiming the right to be the sacrifice. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument.

chapters.title: The King Comes North
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The hollow king marches on the Wolf Reaches with an army and a machine to drain the land itself. Ilse, disgusted, defects and brings the fugitives warning. Emotional beat: a soldier choosing her own side at last.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Reaches
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Battle erupts at the covenant-stone. Yara calls a storm unlike any in living memory while wolf-kin and defected soldiers fight together. Fenris manifests, demanding the price be paid now, mid-battle. Emotional beat: chaos with a terrible deadline.

chapters.title: The Covenant Reforged
chapters.summary: Yara and Soren's shared POV. At the stone, neither will step back—so they give themselves together, splitting the sacrifice between two willing hearts. The covenant accepts the shared bond, binding them to each other and to both realms. Emotional beat: climax; love rewriting the terms of duty.

chapters.title: The Hollow King Falls
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Empowered by the renewed covenant, the land rejects the king's theft; his stolen years burn away, leaving only the old, mortal man beneath. His army kneels or flees. Emotional beat: tyrant unmade not by force but by reclamation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Weather
chapters.summary: Ravn's POV. The wounded are counted; the cost is real. Yara and Soren wake changed—marked, half-heard by both realms, no longer fully belonging to either. Emotional beat: survival's quiet grief and gratitude.

chapters.title: A Crown of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Vellmark lifts its ban; Yara returns openly, reopening the shop, teaching young gifted children control instead of fear. Soren stands beside them, inquisitor's coat traded for an apron. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: The Bridge Between Realms
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, closing. On the anniversary, Yara walks the border at dusk, wolf-song on one side, lamplight on the other, and steps across without fear—for the first time, both worlds are theirs. Emotional beat: resolution; identity chosen, not imposed.
